# From one cell to a whole organism

<!-- STEP id="cell" -->
## Cells

In an earlier chapter, on cells, you learnt that the cell is the basic unit of life. Many cells come together to form a multicellular organism, such as you or a mango tree.

<!-- STEP id="tissue" -->
## Tissues

Cells of a similar type that perform a similar function group together to form a tissue, such as the muscle tissue in the wall of the stomach.

<!-- STEP id="organ" -->
## Organs

More than one type of tissue forms an organ. The stomach has muscle, epithelial and nervous tissue, and blood, working together.

<!-- STEP id="system" -->
## Organ systems

Different organs form an organ system. The stomach works with the mouth, the food pipe and the intestines in the digestive system.

<!-- STEP id="organism" -->
## Organism

Organ systems together form the organism. **In all multicellular organisms there is a hierarchy of organisation: cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and the organism.** A plant follows the same steps: cells, tissues such as xylem and phloem, organs such as the leaf, and the whole plant.

<!-- STEP id="amoeba" -->
## And in an amoeba?

An amoeba is unicellular, so it has no tissues, organs or organ systems. Its one cell is the whole organism and performs all the functions of life.
